title: Why you check work messages at night
series: What your workplace is teaching you

scenes.say: Nobody asked you to check. So why do you?
Most nights, there's nothing new. No emergencies, no replies needed. But once in a while, there's a message that actually matters.
That's an unpredictable reward. And rewards that arrive at random make a habit stubborn.
Then each check relieves a little uncertainty. And that relief rewards checking again.
In one study, just expecting after-hours replies was tied to more anxiety, even when people barely checked email.

right.label: What you felt
right.text: Still anxious, because it was expected

scenes.say: So, is it your habit, or your workplace's unwritten rule? Usually, both.

data.text: Your habit, or your workplace's unwritten rule?
